This integral doesn't look like one of the basic ones. However, we can manipulate the numerator a bit  to make it look more like the denominator, which reveals a more familiar expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}+6}{{x}^{2}+1} & =\frac{{x}^{2}+1-1+6}{{x}^{2}+1} \\  & =\frac{({x}^{2}+1)+5}{{x}^{2}+1} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{{x}^{2}+1}}{\cancel{{x}^{2}+1}}+\frac{5}{{x}^{2}+1} \\  & =1+\frac{5}{{x}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Remembering that

$$
\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\text{d}x=\operatorname{arctan}⁡x,
$$

we can now calculate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+6}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int (1+\frac{5}{{x}^{2}+1})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \text{d}x+\int \frac{5}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \text{d}x+5\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x+5\operatorname{arctan}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
